speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (a) whether an update can be provided on the digital cooperation between Singapore and Indonesia through the Nongsa Digital Park (NDP) and its outlook; (b) whether the cooperation in the NDP special economic zone has led to higher growth for Singapore’s information communication technology sector; and (c) how much has this cooperation led to more jobs and opportunities for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It is good to hear that there are 1,000 tech talents involved.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: But can I ask the Minister of State two supplementary questions?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: First, can the Minister of State elaborate further on the type of sectors that the 250 companies come from?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: My second supplementary question is, can the Minister of State also give us an update on the Nongsa Digital Town she mentioned?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: How is this digital bridge helping Singapore-based companies access the growth of Indonesia's digital economy?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Many will remember it was launched in 2018.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: It has only been five years and for most of the five years, we were mired in the pandemic.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The close proximity of Batam, Bintan, Karimun – which we refer to as the BBK region in short – and the park's status as a Special Economic Zone (SEZ), these two key factors offer our Singapore-based companies advantages to tap the promising growth opportunities of Indonesia's growing digital economy.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: He asked about the profile and the sector.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I will cite a few companies, just to give him a sensing.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Some of these big companies are AIA Singapore, which is an insurance MNC; Infinite Studios, which is a media company; and Infineon, a semi-conductor MNC.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: And another quick example is VA Insight, which is a Singapore-based software engineering company.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: As for his question about other sectors, earlier on in my main reply, I talked about data centres and the three quick examples I shared – GDS Holdings, Princeton Digital Group as well as Gaw Capital – all these are important projects during this time.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: It is a vote of confidence in the potential of the Nongsa Digital Park.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I must specify that there is a difference between the Nongsa Digital Park, under which there is a launch of the Nongsa Digital Town.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The Nongsa Digital Town, if you remember, was only launched two years ago by Minister Chan Chun Sing, in his capacity in the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI), and his counterpart.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The objective of the Nongsa Digital Town really is to further bridge the tech companies and talent in Singapore and Indonesia.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The Nongsa Digital Town will have co-working spaces, digital training centres, offices, lifestyle centres and hotels for business travellers.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We will do so by leveraging the complementary strengths of Singapore and the BBK region – I mentioned the close proximity – and also identify mutually beneficial opportunities in Indonesia's digital economy.
